newsitem.title: DUBAI: Emirates Cable capital to be increased 40 pct.
newsitem.headline: Emirates Cable capital to be increased 40 pct.

text.p: The capital of the new Emirates Cable Co is likely to be raised almost 40 percent to 140 million dirhams ($38 million), the United Arab Emirates Minister of Finance and Industry said in remarks published on Monday.

Sheikh Hamdan bin Rashid al-Maktoum was quoted by newspapers as saying the company -- which will be formed when the Abu Dhabi government takes a share in the majority Dubai government-owned Dubai Cable Co (Ducab) -- would also raise output capacity 35 percent.
Current capacity is 18,000 tonnes of cable, he said.
Last week the official UAE news agency WAM said Abu Dhabi would take a 35 percent share in Ducab, while Britain's BICC Plc will reduce its stake to 30 percent from 40.
Dubai will have 35 percent of the new firm's equity.
Currently, Ducab is a 60-40 joint venture between the Dubai government and BICC.
The UAE is a federation of seven emirates -- the largest and richest of which are Abu Dhabi and Dubai. ($1=3.67 dirhams)
